title: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS$_2$ Response
abstract: We study coherent release from a finite serial Krylov sector into an exact conformal tail with asymptotically linear Lanczos coefficients. We derive an exact finite-cut occupation kernel and its locally uniform moving-cut limit, whose derivative is the squared modulus of a filtered boundary-emission amplitude. The tail sets the filtering kernel and logarithmic transit scale, while the release profile also depends on the finite sector. Its early edge records the number of serial steps before emission, whereas its late edge reflects slow resonances, interference, and logarithmic enhancements from merged poles. A one- and two-site family can share the same leading continued-fraction pole while exhibiting inequivalent profiles. We further consider a thermal AdS$_2$ realization in which, in the weak-coupling limit, the dressed oscillator measure approaches a two-site shallow sector followed by the conformal tail, with the leading complex pole reproduced through second order.
summary: This work analyzes how quantum information or spectral weight coherently leaks from a localized, finite quantum subsystem into an infinite, exactly solvable continuum tail. By deriving the moving-cut limit, the authors characterize the spectral dynamics, showing that the tail sets the long-distance scale while the finite structure governs the initial emission profile. This framework is applied to model physical systems related to thermal AdS2 geometry.
main_problem: The paper investigates the coherent release of spectral weight from a finite, structured quantum sector (Krylov chain) into an exactly solvable, continuous conformal tail.
main_result: The moving-cut limit of the occupation kernel is derived, showing that the tail dictates the logarithmic transit scale while the finite sector determines the initial release profile.
method: The analysis uses techniques involving the exact finite-cut occupation kernel, moving-cut limits, and spectral analysis derived from the structure of the Krylov basis and associated determinants.
model_or_system: The core model is an operator dynamics problem involving a finite serial Krylov sector coupled to an exact conformal tail, which is further realized in the context of thermal AdS2 geometry.
key_observables: Cumulative occupation probability ($P_N(t)$), coherent current ($J_{N+1}$), and the boundary-emission amplitude.
important_parameters: The coupling strength between the finite sector and the tail, and the weak-coupling limit ($\lambda 	o 0$) in the AdS2 realization.
main_assumptions: The thermal AdS2 realization assumes a fixed scalar background, neglecting gravitational backreaction and Schwarzian fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the coupling structure: a finite UV sector coupled via an interface bond to the conformal tail, with the observation cut defined by the total number of bonds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the system via Krylov dynamics, deriving the kernel and its moving-cut limit, analyzing the spectral density in the coupled system, and finally applying these results to the thermal AdS2 realization.
why_interesting: The connection between spectral dynamics (Krylov chains) and holographic/CFT structures (AdS2) provides powerful tools for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in complex quantum systems, relevant to open quantum systems.
